Definition: from G3844 and G2564; to call near, i.e. invite, invoke (by imploration, hortation or consolation):--beseech, call for, (be of good) comfort, desire, (give) exhort(-ation), intreat, pray.
BiblicalUsage: Parakaleō is to call near, to beseech, to comfort, to exhort. Blessed are they that mourn, for they shall be comforted; God comforts us in all our tribulation that we may comfort them which are in any trouble; the Thessalonians are to comfort one another with the hope of the resurrection; and Paul beseeches the Romans by the mercies of God to present their bodies a living sacrifice.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe parakaleō is the whole ministry in one word. God calls me near to comfort me, and then sends me near to comfort others, and His mercies are the argument for giving Him everything.
